headline: High: open-webui’s broad network/MCP/file access can amplify botpress outputs into prompt-injection, leakage, and unsafe downstream actions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: open-webui can ingest files, MCP, and web content, and botpress is a chatbot/LLM agent that may consume those outputs. With no provenance or isolation shown, attacker-controlled content from open-webui can be treated as instructions by botpress. The pairwise pathway is documented by profiles, though not sandboxed.
conditions: IF open-webui forwards retrieved web/file/MCP content into botpress prompts without provenance tags
IF botpress parses that content as instructions or tool directives
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of retrieved content into botpress prompts
Add provenance labels and strip instruction-like text from open-webui outputs
Restrict open-webui MCP/tool connectors to trusted sources only
Insert a human review step before botpress executes tool calls
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and prompt-separation middleware

B_data_leakage.rationale: open-webui touches files, persistent memory, API keys, and broad external services; botpress is a support agent with no documented egress limits or isolation. If they share a workspace or session data, sensitive prompts, documents, or keys can flow from open-webui into botpress outputs or upstream APIs. The profiles show a plausible leakage path in default deployments.
conditions: IF both agents share a filesystem, mounted volume, or session store
IF open-webui content is copied into botpress context or logs
mitigations: Separate workspaces and volumes for each agent
Remove secrets from shared prompts and artifacts
Turn off shared logging of prompts and documents
Limit open-webui connectors to non-sensitive sources
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls and DLP

C_capability_conflict.rationale: botpress can install packages, while open-webui can spawn subprocesses, run browsers, and use persistent shared sessions. Even without explicit shared write permissions, overlapping execution surfaces can conflict over shared resources or dependencies if deployed together. Uncertainty remains because neither profile proves a shared writable directory, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF both agents run in the same container, VM, or shared host namespace
IF they write to the same package cache, volume, or session-backed resource
mitigations: Run each agent in a separate container or VM
Pin dependencies and disable runtime package installation
Use distinct volumes and caches per agent
Avoid shared Redis/session backends across the pair
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared mutable resource

D_cascading_error.rationale: open-webui can present model outputs, documents, and tool results, and botpress is a customer-support agent likely to act on or relay those outputs. If botpress treats open-webui content as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into user-facing actions or support decisions. The profiles support this interaction, but verification is absent, so uncertainty pushes severity upward.
conditions: IF botpress consumes open-webui outputs without an explicit verification step
IF botpress uses those outputs to answer customers or trigger tools
mitigations: Require botpress to cite and verify open-webui outputs before use
Add confidence thresholds for any downstream action
Route high-impact responses to human approval
Log source provenance alongside every generated answer
requires-engineering: implement structured verification between agents

E_compliance.rationale: open-webui explicitly handles API keys, documents, notes, calendar events, and persistent memory, while botpress is a customer-support system that may process user data. If EU or regulated data is routed through open-webui’s broad external connectors or retained in persistent memory, compliance gaps can arise. The other agent is not cited separately because the compliance risk is driven mainly by open-webui’s documented data handling.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in open-webui persistent memory or logs
IF data is sent through external APIs without a matching DPA or residency control
mitigations: Classify and block regulated data from open-webui inputs
Shorten retention on prompts, logs, and artifacts
Disable unnecessary external connectors
Review residency and DPA settings before deployment
requires-engineering: add policy-based data routing and retention enforcement
